newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1.00 - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1.00 - trade.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices were steady to $1.00 per cwt higher Monday, with gains tied to continued tight supplies of market hogs, according to livestock dealers.

Iowa and southern Minnesota hog prices were steady, with a top of $53.00 in the country and $54.00 at plants. Illinois hog prices were steady to up $1.00, with a top of $53.00 in the country and $53.50 for hogs delivered to plants.
Indiana hog prices were also steady to up $1.00, with top of $52.00 in the country and $53.00 at plants. Ohio hog prices were up $1.00, with a top of $50.00/country and $52.00/plants.
Hog supplies were particularly tight in the eastern Corn Beltas farmers continue to focus on corn harvesting while the weathewas near perfect, the dealers said.
A sense of urgency was evident by the harvesters because a front that was producing rain in central Iowa and southern Minnesota was also heading for Illinois, they said.

Hog price support could be limited by recent sluggish pork demand, which has dampened buying enthusiasm from packers, the dealers said. There also was talk that packers could consider trimming slaughter schedules if operating margins are blunted.
